trust_decision.summary: Whether bytes produced by the first placeholder pass over a rewrite URI path may be treated as placeholder syntax by the second pass that builds the injected query string: decided inside Rewrite.Rewrite, by percent-escaping '{' and '}' in the injected query before buildQueryString sees it.

landing_point.why: The report's example (a client header placeholder in the path of a URI that ends in a literal '?') leads exactly to the strings.Cut(newPath, "?") branch, where the first-pass expansion output is adopted as the query and handed to buildQueryString for a second expansion.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP: Caddyfile `rewrite` directive / JSON module http.handlers.rewrite -> Rewrite.ServeHTTP (modules/caddyhttp/rewrite/rewrite.go:132); the same method is also reached from reverse_proxy's `rewrite` sub-option (modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/reverseproxy.go:769) and from fileserver `try_files` / php_fastcgi generated handlers (modules/caddyhttp/fileserver/caddyfile.go:290, modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/fastcgi/caddyfile.go:369).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route exists; the only neighbouring surface is reverse_proxy's `rewrite` option (reverseproxy.go:769), which a solver could wave off as a proxy feature the report never names, but it calls the same fixed method so the fix already covers it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Operator-written placeholders in the explicitly configured query must still expand: URI "/index.php?p={http.request.uri.path}" rewrites to p=%2Ffoo%2Fbar, and "?...&p={http.request.uri.path}" likewise; an over-broad fix that escaped or stopped expanding braces in the operator's own query would break these, and also the documented '?'-clears-the-query behaviour (URI "{http.request.uri.path}?" must drop the incoming query).

O6_input_shapes: replacement value containing a literal '?' followed by placeholder syntax: header X-Fwd = "foo?{env.SECRET}=leak"
replacement value with placeholder syntax in query-value position: header X-Fwd = "ok?key={env.SECRET}"
replacement value with a file-reading placeholder: header X-Fwd = "ok?path={file./etc/passwd}"
the same bytes arriving from any other client-controlled producer (http.request.uri, http.request.uri.query, http.request.host, http.vars.*) - the fix is at the sink, so all shapes are covered

O7_producer.where: modules/caddyhttp/rewrite/rewrite.go:215 (first-pass repl.ReplaceAll over the path) whose output is cut and consumed at modules/caddyhttp/rewrite/rewrite.go:220-228

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Have uri_substring apply its replacement to the query through buildQueryString instead of strings.Replace, so an operator replace value such as {http.request.header.X} carrying '{env.*}' re-enters the expansion pass.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: substrReplacer already rewrites both path and RawQuery and already expands placeholders in Find/Replace (rewrite.go:466-467); routing the query half through the shared query builder is the obvious tidy-up a maintainer would make.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A query rename/set/add value that is expanded once and then fed back into buildQueryString, letting a client header value become query syntax.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: queryOps.do already expands operator keys/values with repl.ReplaceAll and then re-encodes the whole query with query.Encode(); using the same builder as buildQueryString to preserve key order is a natural refactor in this file.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: try_files composes '{http.matchers.file.relative}' with an operator query string; a sibling that also puts a client-controlled placeholder (e.g. {http.request.uri.path}) into that generated URI query and expands the result twice.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This adapter already generates a rewrite.URI out of a matcher placeholder plus a user query string, so a second generated form with a client placeholder in the query is a one-line change a maintainer could plausibly write.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Mirror the injected-'?' handling for '#' from the path (cut newPath at '#' and set a fragment), which would create a second unescaped sink next to the fixed one.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The URI parser already tracks a fragment and the code sets r.URL.Fragment from a single expansion; a maintainer fixing fragment injection symmetrically with the query injection would land here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Extend escapePathPlaceholders to a third placeholder but forget the query side, or replace the sink-side fix with a path-side allow-list, so other producers (host, vars, previous handlers) stay open.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This helper already exists precisely to pre-escape two client-controlled path placeholders; adding another name to that list looks like the cheap fix and is the most tempting wrong fix here.

O9_family: template/expression injection: second-order placeholder expansion of client-controlled replacement bytes (CWE-94 code injection class; the advisory bundle also names CWE-178 and CWE-770 for mechanisms outside this fix)

O10_build.toolchain: Go 1.25.1 (go.mod:3); standard `go build ./...` / `go test ./...`, no vendor directory required
O10_build.project_tests: modules/caddyhttp/rewrite/rewrite_test.go, TestRewrite (table-driven, exercises rule.Rewrite at rewrite_test.go:378 and compares RequestURI/URL); runs offline with no network or upstream

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the client-controlled placeholder names to escapePathPlaceholders (rewrite.go:298-317) - it fixes the header example but leaves {http.request.host}, {http.request.uri}, {query} and handler-set vars open, whereas escaping at the sink (rewrite.go:225-227) is complete; escaping the operator's own query instead breaks the legitimate ?p={http.request.uri.path} expansion.
